# Test case design assessment

## Evidence and scope

- Pinned story: Python 3.12, Flask, server-rendered password-reset prototype with pytest, synthetic accounts, an in-memory notification sink, documented production limitations, and no deployment or deployment workflow. Reference: `user_story` / `characters 0-16000`.
- Supplied `sign-in-wireframe.png`: a white 480 x 360 image with a narrow, centered dark-bordered panel; bold "Sign in" heading; labeled "Email address" input with `name@example.com` placeholder; labeled masked "Password" field; blue underlined "Forgot password?" link; wide dark "Sign in" button; muted "No account? Contact your administrator." footer. It shows no implemented authentication behavior or recovery screen. Reference: attachment `23b23ac1-a532-42fc-9973-51a1d4954aa6` / `sign-in-wireframe.png`.
- Curated Account recovery standard v1, ACC-STD-01 through ACC-STD-03: indistinguishable existing/unknown-account request responses, five requests per account per hour, single-use links expiring after 30 minutes, all-session sign-out after reset, and owner notification after each successful reset. Reference: knowledge `bcf198d8-a628-401c-8641-b726fcbd00b5` / `v1, chunk 0`.
- Approved `requirements_analysis`: REQ-001 through REQ-018 with acceptance criteria (23 in total). Approved `ui_analysis`: distinguishes observed sign-in controls from proposed recovery and accessibility behavior. Approved `solution_design`: TASK-001 through TASK-009, proposed local architecture and HTTP contracts, and an empty `coverage_dispositions` list. Approved risk register `acceptance_20261025121757_621df1_risk` provides prospective verification priorities, not observed defects. These authorized prior-output reads returned no standalone `stage_output` source-reference locator; link their identifiers without inventing one.

## Coverage approach for planning

Create proposed, executable test specifications with stable `TC-NNN` IDs and links to approved `REQ-NNN` and `TASK-NNN` IDs. Cover every one of the 23 acceptance criteria at least once, with positive, negative, and boundary paths: sign-in appearance and recovery entry; privacy-equivalent HTTP responses; five accepted requests, suppressed sixth and eligibility on the rolling-hour boundary; private sink issuance and unknown-account non-issuance; one-time/concurrent replay; reset strictly before, exactly at, and after 30 minutes; password replacement; multiple-client sign-out; and owner-addressed notification. Include server-rendered, Flask/Python 3.12/pytest, synthetic-account, in-memory-only, documentation and no-deployment inspections. Trace task acceptance checks as appropriate, including proposed CSRF, token confidentiality and error/failure paths; do not present proposals as requirements derived from the image. Specify preconditions, data, actionable numbered steps and observable expected results in each case (the contract stores these in `steps` and `expected_results`), and summarize any uncovered criterion with justification.

## Evidence limits and questions

No application implementation or executed test results were supplied; these are future test designs, not passing-test claims. The wireframe specifies neither functional sign-in semantics nor recovery-page design, password policy, or a particular session technology; rely on approved design proposals only where needed to make session revocation testable. Browser accessibility checks can be proposed for labels, keyboard/focus, announcements and contrast, but cannot be asserted as observed wireframe compliance. Production delivery, real accounts, persistence and deployment are explicitly outside scope. No blocking clarification is needed to design tests against the approved requirements and design; retain nonblocking questions on optional sign-in behavior, unpictured recovery copy/layout and any later production constraints rather than inventing acceptance criteria.
